title: Register minimum loop
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers, let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to each of $d$ indices and bit strings, and let $y$ be a bit string. Choose pairwise distinct registers $t,a,b$ and states $\mathrm{test}_1,\mathrm{test}_2,\mathrm{bump},\mathrm{yes},\mathrm{no}$ so that the program branches from $\mathrm{test}_1$ to $\mathrm{yes}$ when register $t$ equals register $a$, and otherwise to $\mathrm{test}_2$; from $\mathrm{test}_2$ it branches to $\mathrm{no}$ when $t=b$, and otherwise to $\mathrm{bump}$; and at $\mathrm{bump}$ it increments $t$ and returns to $\mathrm{test}_1$. If the initial register values $v$ are all at most $B$, and $v(t)\le v(a)$ and $v(t)\le v(b)$, then the program reaches the state selected by whether $v(a)\le v(b)$, with register $t$ replaced by $\min(v(a),v(b))$ and every other register unchanged; throughout the run, the program satisfies the guard requiring its register values to remain at most $B$ and its configurations to satisfy the program's precondition.

t, a, b are pairwise distinct registers
A(test₁) compares t with a, branching to yes on equality and test₂ otherwise

A(bump) increments t and returns to test₁

v is an initial register valuation
